verdict: Cognizant grew revenue 5% to $5.66B on a 12% jump in Financial Services work, while $51M of restructuring costs from its Project Leap overhaul held the GAAP operating margin at 15.4%.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +4.6% YoY, or +4.8% in constant currency (stripping out exchange-rate moves)

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $0.56 a year ago, when a one-time tax charge cut EPS by $0.80; adjusted EPS was $1.49, up 7.2%

kpis.label: Financial Services revenue
kpis.note: +12.0% YoY — the star segment, 31% of all revenue

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: Operating cash flow of $1,004M less $79M of capital spending in the quarter

segments.name: Financial Services
segments.note: Tech services for banks, insurers and other financial firms — the biggest segment, and the growth engine this quarter.

segments.name: Health Sciences
segments.note: Tech services for hospitals, health insurers and drug and medical-device makers. Revenue slipped slightly, down 1.1%.

segments.name: Products and Resources
segments.note: Tech services for manufacturers, retailers, energy and travel and hospitality companies. Revenue slipped 0.9%.

segments.name: Communications, Media and Technology
segments.note: Tech services for telecom, media and technology companies. Growth included a boost from recently bought businesses.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling the work and running the company — sales teams, management, finance and admin.

opex.name: Restructuring charges
opex.note: Project Leap restructuring — the cost of reshaping the workforce and operating model. See one-off items below.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Wear and tear on offices, equipment and software, spread over their working lives, plus amortization of bought intangibles (assets like customer contracts from deals).

otherDetail: Net other expense was $8M in total: $19M of interest expense and $8M of other costs, partly offset by $16M of interest income, $2M of currency gains and a $1M gain from equity-method investments (shares in other companies accounted for by picking up a slice of their profit). The statement shows other income (expense), net of -$9M plus the separate +$1M equity-method line, which the flow carries as equityM.

takeaways.title: Financial Services carried the growth
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 4.6% to $5.66B. Financial Services jumped 12.0% to $1.77B and Communications, Media and Technology rose 10.5% to $939M, while Health Sciences fell 1.1% and Products and Resources fell 0.9%. Trailing 12-month bookings were $28.7B, up 4%.

takeaways.title: Restructuring held back the margin
takeaways.text: Operating income was $872M, a 15.4% margin, down from 16.0% a year ago. The $51M of Project Leap restructuring charges explains the gap: leaving those out, the company's adjusted operating margin was 16.3%, up from 16.0%.

takeaways.title: EPS more than doubled — off a low base
takeaways.text: Net income was $627M and GAAP EPS $1.39, up from $0.56 a year ago. That comparison flatters the quarter: a year ago a one-time, non-cash tax charge cut EPS by $0.80. Adjusted EPS, which strips out such items, rose a steadier 7.2% to $1.49.

oneTimers: Operating costs include $51M of restructuring charges for Project Leap, a program launched in Q2 2026 to reshape Cognizant's operating model around AI — funding new offerings and partnerships and reshaping the workforce. The company now expects total Project Leap costs of $180M–$250M, with $140M–$160M of that in 2026.
footerNote: All figures are as reported in $M in the statement of operations.
follow100Note: The $1M equity-method gain sits below the tax line on Cognizant's statement; it is carried separately so operating income, other income and tax tie exactly to the reported $627M net income.
